subject: histology
prompt: A large conducting-airway wall has respiratory epithelium, abundant seromucous glands, and a broad hyaline-cartilage band, without surrounding lung parenchyma. Which organ is this?
explanation: The combination of ciliated pseudostratified epithelium, submucosal seromucous glands, and a broad outer hyaline-cartilage band without surrounding lung parenchyma identifies trachea.

distractorExplanations.B: A bronchus has discontinuous cartilage plates and a more conspicuous circumferential smooth-muscle layer.
distractorExplanations.C: A terminal bronchiole has no cartilage and no submucosal glands.
distractorExplanations.D: The esophagus has stratified squamous epithelium and lacks airway cartilage and respiratory epithelium.

learningObjective: Identify trachea at low power from its complete wall architecture.

subject: histology
prompt: Which epithelial cell in this tracheal lining contacts the basement membrane but normally does not reach the lumen?
explanation: Basal cells are short progenitor cells seated on the basement membrane. Their nuclei help create the pseudostratified appearance, but their apical surface does not reach the lumen.

distractorExplanations.A: Ciliated cells extend from the basement membrane to the lumen and bear apical motile cilia.
distractorExplanations.C: Goblet cells reach the lumen and release mucin onto the epithelial surface.
distractorExplanations.D: Brush cells reach the lumen and carry short apical microvilli.

learningObjective: Recognize the basal-cell compartment of respiratory epithelium.

prompt: Which sequence correctly follows this tracheal wall from the lumen outward?

Hyaline cartilage → respiratory epithelium → lamina propria → glands
Respiratory epithelium → lamina propria → seromucous glands → perichondrium → hyaline cartilage
Respiratory epithelium → skeletal muscle → glands → elastic cartilage

epithelium lamina propria glands perichondrium cartilage

distractorExplanations.B: Cartilage is an outer supporting layer, not the luminal lining.
distractorExplanations.D: Trachea has smooth trachealis muscle posteriorly and hyaline, not elastic, cartilage.

distractorExplanations.A: Parathyroid is arranged in solid cords of chief and oxyphil cells and lacks colloid-filled follicles.
distractorExplanations.C: Pituitary shows endocrine cell cords and neurosecretory tissue rather than follicles.
distractorExplanations.D: Adrenal has a zonated cortex and medulla, not colloid-filled follicles.

learningObjective: Identify thyroid gland from follicular architecture.

subject: histology
prompt: What is the main hormone-precursor protein stored in the follicular colloid?
explanation: Follicular cells synthesize thyroglobulin and release it apically into the lumen, where iodinated residues serve as stored precursors for T3 and T4.

distractorExplanations.A: Calcitonin is secreted by parafollicular cells and is not stored as the bulk follicular colloid.
distractorExplanations.B: PTH is made by parathyroid chief cells, not thyroid follicles.
distractorExplanations.D: Albumin is a plasma protein and is not the specialized thyroid hormone precursor.

learningObjective: Explain the composition and role of thyroid colloid.

subject: histology
prompt: Which cell produces calcitonin and normally does not contact the follicular lumen?
explanation: Parafollicular or C cells lie basally within follicular epithelium or in small interfollicular groups and secrete calcitonin toward capillaries.

distractorExplanations.A: Follicular cells line the lumen and produce thyroglobulin and thyroid hormones.
distractorExplanations.B: Chief cells are the principal hormone-producing cells of parathyroid gland.
distractorExplanations.C: Oxyphil cells occur in parathyroid and do not produce calcitonin.

learningObjective: Differentiate follicular and parafollicular thyroid cells.

prompt: Long parallel unbranched fibers show clear cross-striations and multiple nuclei at their periphery. Which tissue is this?
explanation: Long cylindrical fibers, striking cross-striations, and multiple peripheral nuclei are diagnostic of skeletal muscle.

distractorExplanations.B: Cardiac fibers branch, usually have central nuclei, and are joined by intercalated discs.
distractorExplanations.C: Smooth muscle has spindle-shaped cells and no cross-striations.
distractorExplanations.D: Tendon has parallel collagen bundles and flattened fibroblast nuclei but no muscle striations.

learningObjective: Identify skeletal muscle in longitudinal section.

subject: histology
prompt: Why can one skeletal muscle fiber contain many peripheral nuclei?

options.text: It repeatedly divides by mitosis after birth
It forms by fusion of many myoblasts into a syncytium
Each nucleus belongs to a separate cell
The nuclei are actually Schwann cells

acceptedFreeText: It forms by fusion of many myoblasts into a syncytium
explanation: Developing myoblasts fuse to form a long multinucleated myotube. The resulting myonuclei are displaced to the periphery beneath the sarcolemma.

distractorExplanations.A: Mature skeletal muscle fibers are highly differentiated and do not routinely undergo mitosis.
distractorExplanations.C: The nuclei lie within one continuous muscle fiber cytoplasm.
distractorExplanations.D: Schwann-cell nuclei accompany nerves, not the numerous myonuclei beneath the sarcolemma.

learningObjective: Relate skeletal muscle development to multinucleation.

prompt: Which finding in this image is most useful for excluding cardiac muscle?

options.text: Multiple nuclei located at the fiber periphery

acceptedFreeText: Multiple nuclei located at the fiber periphery
explanation: Multiple peripheral nuclei strongly favor skeletal muscle. Cardiac myocytes usually have one central nucleus and branch at intercalated discs.

distractorExplanations.A: Both skeletal and cardiac muscle are striated.
distractorExplanations.B: Both skeletal and cardiac muscle are strongly eosinophilic on H&E.
distractorExplanations.D: Both muscle types have delicate connective tissue around fibers or cells.

learningObjective: Differentiate skeletal from cardiac muscle histologically.

prompt: Striated fibers branch, contain central nuclei, and meet at dark transverse cell junctions. Which tissue is shown?
explanation: Branching striated cells with central nuclei and intercalated discs identify cardiac muscle.

distractorExplanations.A: Skeletal fibers are long, unbranched, multinucleated, and have peripheral nuclei.
distractorExplanations.B: Smooth muscle lacks cross-striations and intercalated discs.
distractorExplanations.C: Dense regular connective tissue contains collagen bundles rather than branching striated cells.

subject: histology
prompt: What are the dark transverse lines joining adjacent cardiac myocytes?
explanation: Intercalated discs are step-like junctional complexes at cardiac cell boundaries and appear as prominent dark transverse lines.

distractorExplanations.B: Z discs repeat within every sarcomere and appear as much finer regular striations.
distractorExplanations.C: Nodes of Ranvier are gaps in myelin along axons.
distractorExplanations.D: Myotendinous junctions link muscle to tendon rather than one cardiac cell to the next.

learningObjective: Recognize intercalated discs on light microscopy.

subject: histology
prompt: Which component of an intercalated disc provides low-resistance electrical coupling between cardiac myocytes?
explanation: Gap junction channels allow ions to pass directly between myocytes, electrically coupling the myocardium; adherens junctions and desmosomes provide mechanical coupling.

distractorExplanations.A: Desmosomes provide strong mechanical adhesion but do not directly pass ionic current.
distractorExplanations.C: Fasciae adherentes anchor actin filaments and transmit contractile force.
distractorExplanations.D: Tight junctions form permeability barriers and are not the main electrical couplers in myocardium.

learningObjective: Connect intercalated-disc structure to electrical syncytium behavior.

subject: histology
prompt: Densely packed parallel eosinophilic bundles contain sparse rows of flattened nuclei and no cross-striations. Which tissue is this?
explanation: Parallel type I collagen bundles with sparse flattened tenocyte nuclei identify dense regular connective tissue of tendon.

distractorExplanations.A: Skeletal muscle has striated fibers and multiple peripheral myonuclei.
distractorExplanations.B: Fibrocartilage contains rounded chondrocytes in lacunae among collagen bundles.
distractorExplanations.D: Peripheral nerve has axons, myelin spaces, and perineurial fascicles.

learningObjective: Identify tendon in longitudinal section.

subject: histology
prompt: Which cell produces and maintains the parallel type I collagen bundles in this tendon?
explanation: Tenocytes are elongated specialized fibroblasts aligned between collagen bundles; their compressed nuclei appear as thin dark profiles.

distractorExplanations.A: Chondrocytes occupy lacunae within cartilage matrix.
distractorExplanations.B: Osteocytes occupy lacunae in mineralized bone.
distractorExplanations.C: Myocytes are contractile muscle cells and do not form the tendon collagen bundles.

learningObjective: Identify the principal resident cell of tendon.

subject: histology
prompt: Which microscopic property contributes most to the slow healing of an injured tendon?
explanation: Dense collagen, sparse resident cells, and limited vascularity slow delivery of repair cells and matrix turnover after tendon injury.

distractorExplanations.B: Tendon is relatively poorly vascularized rather than rich in sinusoids.
distractorExplanations.C: Tenocytes have limited proliferative activity in the dense collagenous matrix.
distractorExplanations.D: Tendon is not mineralized; its dense collagen and limited blood supply are the key issues.

learningObjective: Relate tendon histology to its limited repair capacity.
